issues.failure_explanation: T is assumed to be a diffeomorphism from the k-dimensional manifold M onto supp(T_#mu) = T(M), so supp(T_#mu) is a k-dimensional submanifold of R^d. Whenever d > k - a regime the paper explicitly allows (d >= k) and uses in all experiments (latent dimensions 30/100 with lower intrinsic dimension) - T(M) has d-dimensional Lebesgue measure zero, and a probability measure supported on a Lebesgue-null set cannot be absolutely continuous w.r.t. Lebesgue measure on R^d. The claimed density rho_T(x)dx on R^d therefore does not exist unless d = k.

issues.why_classification: The claim is flatly false in the paper's operating regime and is load-bearing for later proofs, so it is more than a typo; but every affected statement survives once densities are taken on the k-dimensional image, so the repair is a contained restatement of the setup rather than new proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated implication is false. Take alpha = gamma = 1/2 and a pair with ||x-x'||^2 = 2 = (1-alpha)/(alpha*gamma), so (x,x') in tilde A. The weak condition only forces -0.25 <= ||T(x)-T(x')||^2 <= 11, so a two-point map with ||T(x)-T(x')||^2 = 0 satisfies the weak condition on A = {(x,x')} but violates the claimed lower bound alpha(1-gamma)||x-x'||^2 = 0.5; likewise ||T(x)-T(x')||^2 = 11 satisfies the weak condition but violates the claimed upper bound (1/alpha+gamma)||x-x'||^2 = 5. Solving the weak lower bound for the claimed form requires ||x-x'||^2 >= (1-alpha^2)/(alpha(alpha-1+gamma)), which is larger than (1-alpha)/(alpha*gamma), and when alpha + gamma*alpha^2 <= 1 no separation threshold yields the claimed upper bound at all. No proof of the proposition is given anywhere in the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate with correct constants (e.g., on ||x-x'||^2 >= (1-alpha^2)/(alpha^2 gamma), alpha^2(1-gamma)||x-x'||^2 <= ||T(x)-T(x')||^2 <= (1+gamma)alpha^{-2}||x-x'||^2) and supply the short derivation.
issues.overall_effect: prop:added-1 is false as stated; the later informal statement that the weak condition 'implies the regular bi-Lipschitz condition for well-separated pairs of points' loses its stated quantitative content. No labelled downstream result cites the proposition.

issues.why_classification: The statement is false as written and there is no single forced correction (several inequivalent repaired versions exist, and no proof is present), so it is not a pure typo; but the repair is local routine algebra and nothing else in the paper depends on the result, so the loss is contained.

issues.failure_explanation: In the natural uniform topology (the one in which the GME cost is continuous and Arzela-Ascoli gives relative compactness of normalized beta-Lipschitz maps), the invertibility requirement in T_beta is not closed: e.g., with M = S^1 and d = 2, the embeddings T_n(theta) = (cos(theta)-1, n^{-1}sin(theta)) are invertible, 1-Lipschitz, and satisfy T_n(0) = 0, but converge uniformly to the non-injective map theta -> (cos(theta)-1, 0). Hence T_beta is not compact, and the asserted existence of a minimizer is unproven.

issues.failure_explanation: The second variation equals the integral of <h, nabla^2_{xx}c h> against T_#mu, so it evaluates h only on T(M), a compact proper subset of R^d (indeed k-dimensional). For any nonzero h vanishing on T(M), delta^2 L_rec(h,h) = 0 while alpha^d c_min rho_min ||h||^2_{L^2(R^d)} > 0, so the lower bound is false and the cost is not strongly convex in the stated norm; the change-of-variables chain cannot yield a full-space L^2(R^d) lower bound because the integrand is supported on T(M). For the same reason the minimizer is not unique: L_rec evaluates S only on T(M), so every extension of T^{-1} off T(M) attains zero cost, contradicting the claimed unique solution. When k < d the upper bound in the same norm also fails (a unit bump supported in a shrinking tube around the k-dimensional T(M) has fixed integral against T_#mu but vanishing L^2(R^d) norm).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate thm:S-2 with support-restricted norms, e.g. L^2 over T(M) with respect to the volume measure, giving Hessian bounds [alpha^k c_min rho_min, alpha^{-k} c_max rho_max], claim uniqueness only of the restriction of S to T(M), and restate cor:conv-rate in the same support norm.
issues.overall_effect: The Hessian bound eq:st-l2loss and the uniqueness/strong-convexity assertions fail as stated; consequently cor:conv-rate's linear convergence to 'the' minimizer S^{(*)} with contraction 1 - alpha^{2d} c_min rho_min/(c_max rho_max) in an unspecified norm is unsupported (the strong-convexity constant is invalid, and the limit minimizer is not unique).
issues.title: Decoder strong convexity and uniqueness claimed in a norm the cost cannot control
issues.why_classification: Two labelled results must be restated and false uniqueness/strong-convexity claims corrected - more than a routine edit - but the corrected versions are standard and preserve the paper's message that decoder conditioning improves as alpha approaches 1; no central claim is abandoned.

issues.failure_explanation: For a probability measure, Holder gives integral of g^p <= (integral of g^{p'})^{p/p'}, not integral of g^p <= integral of g^{p'} as used (false whenever g takes values below 1, e.g. g = 1/2 with p=1, p'=2). Because the reconstruction cost uses exponent p', the reconstruction error actually enters the W_p bound with power 1/p' and Jacobian power alpha^{-d/p'}, not the stated alpha^{-d/p}(epsilon_rec+epsilon)^{1/p}; since epsilon_rec^{1/p'} >= epsilon_rec^{1/p} for epsilon_rec <= 1, the stated bound is stronger than what the proof establishes. The same root appears in cor:generative-map3: its W_1 argument needs integral ||tilde S - S|| dR_#nu <= (integral ||tilde S - S||^2 dR_#nu)^{1/2}, producing a term of order epsilon_rec^{1/2}, not the linear-in-epsilon_rec term written in its statement.

issues.failure_explanation: lem:S-discrete and prop:discrete-cont are Bernstein concentration bounds for a fixed map chosen independently of the sample. In the main theorems they are applied to maps obtained by minimizing empirical costs on the same sample: the decoder S with L_rec(S, hat mu_n) < epsilon_rec is trained on hat mu_n (per the GPE framework), and the encoder T is explicitly taken as a minimizer of hatGME(T, hat mu_n) in cor:generative-map3's proof and is fed through prop:discrete-cont and prop:T-discrete-cont. For such data-dependent maps the pointwise concentration statements do not apply, and no uniform-over-class bound is established. The same root affects the step E W_p(T_#mu, T_#hat mu_n) <= C_2 n^{-2/(d+4)}, where the cited Horowitz-Karandikar result requires i.i.d. samples from a fixed distribution, not a sample-dependent T.

issues.failure_explanation: For T : M -> R^d with M k-dimensional, nabla T is a d-by-k matrix, so det(nabla T nabla T^T) is the determinant of a d-by-d matrix of rank at most k and is identically 0 when k < d; the correct Jacobian of the change of variables is sqrt(det(nabla T^T nabla T)) <= K^k. The stated bound K^d is strictly smaller than K^k when K < 1, so the lemma's conclusion fails for contracting encoders (the hypothesis allows any K > 0; e.g., a 1-dimensional M, d = 2, K = 1/2 makes the displayed density bound too small by a factor K^{k-d} = 2 and the lemma's inequality can be saturated at the larger true value). The same wrong formula appears in thm:S-2's proof and produces cor:generative-map3's factors beta^d, which are invalid in the regime beta < 1 that prop:T-discrete-cont explicitly permits.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the correct Jacobian sqrt(det(nabla T^T nabla T)) with exponent k throughout; statements whose base is at least 1 (thm:generative-map's use with K = 1/alpha, and alpha^{+-d} bounds) are unchanged, while cor:generative-map3's beta^d factors become beta^k.
issues.overall_effect: lem:rec-bound is false as stated for K < 1; cor:generative-map3's beta^d factors are wrong whenever beta < 1 and d > k; the density displays in thm:S-2's proof use a determinant that vanishes identically when k < d.
issues.title: Wrong Jacobian determinant in the change of variables; exponent K^d fails for contractions
issues.why_classification: The correction is a forced formula change (not a typo: it alters exponents and cor:generative-map3's stated beta-dependence in the beta < 1 regime) and propagates to three proofs, but all final statements otherwise survive, so the loss is limited.

issues.failure_explanation: Bernstein's inequality with t = epsilon*diam(M)^p, b <= diam(M)^p, sigma^2 <= diam(M)^{2p} yields failure probability 2 exp(-n epsilon^2/(6(1+epsilon/3))), exactly as the lemma's own proof derives. The statement instead claims 2 exp(-n epsilon/(6(1+epsilon/3))). For epsilon < 1 the claimed failure probability is smaller than the proved one, i.e. the stated guarantee is stronger than what is established; thm:generative-map repeats the same wrong exponent in its statement and proof.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace epsilon by epsilon^2 in the exponent in lem:S-discrete's statement and in thm:generative-map's probability, matching the proof and the analogous prop:discrete-cont.
issues.overall_effect: The confidence attached to lem:S-discrete, and repeated in thm:generative-map, is overstated for epsilon < 1; the correct exponent in the probability is quadratic in epsilon.
issues.title: Stated probability of the reconstruction concentration lemma contradicts its own proof
issues.why_classification: The single forced correction is dictated by the lemma's own proof; the bound's form and the exponential-in-n concentration guarantee are preserved, with no other mathematical change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Define a transport plan $\gamma\in\Pi(\hat\mu_n, \nu)$ and $\gamma_T \in \Pi(T_\#\hat\mu_n, T_\#\nu)$ such that $\gamma_T$ is defined as $\gamma_T(x,y) = \gamma(T(x),T(y))$.
Let $\hat\mu_n = \frac{1}{n} \sum^n_{i=1}\delta_{x_i}$ be an empirical distribution from $\mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: The step bounds gamma(M^2 \ A) by rho_max nu_max L^2(M^2 \ A), i.e., it treats the coupling as having a joint density bounded by rho_max nu_max with respect to L^2. But the lemma takes gamma in Pi(hat mu_n, nu), whose first marginal is the discrete empirical measure with no Lebesgue density: e.g., gamma = delta_{x_0} x nu with M^2 \ A containing {x_0} x B and nu(B) = 1 gives gamma(M^2 \ A) = 1 while rho_max nu_max L^2(M^2 \ A) = 0, since the slice {x_0} x B is L^2-null. A correct derivation must bound gamma(A^c) <= nu_max (1/n) sum_i L(A^c_{x_i}) and then control that empirical average (whose mean is at most rho_max L^2(A^c)) by an additional concentration argument that is missing. The lemma's stated event therefore does not follow as written, and cor:generative-map3 invokes it with first marginal hat mu_n.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the extra concentration step for (1/n) sum_i L(A^c_{x_i}) (Bernstein), adding an O(epsilon)-type term - absorbable into the existing '+ epsilon' in cor:generative-map3's bound - and worsening the probability constants accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: lem:D-d-bound, and hence lem:D-d-Wasserstein and the GME-cost term of cor:generative-map3's bound, are unproven in the empirical-marginal setting in which they are used.
issues.title: Mass of the bad set under a coupling with an empirical marginal is bounded by a nonexistent joint density
issues.why_classification: The lemma needs an additional standard concentration argument and a small restatement, a contained repair; the final theorem's form and rate survive, so the mathematical loss is limited.
